Estimate an n-gram transition network analysis model

Source: R/build_aliases.R
build_ngram.Rd

build_network(method = "ngram"), or for short build_ngram(), estimates an n-gram transition network analysis model from windows of n_gram consecutive states. Each window adds each of its adjacent pairs once, so a pair inside a sequence is counted up to n_gram - 1 times, as tna::build_model(type = "n-gram") counts it.

The weights are raw counts; add scaling = "normalize" for row probabilities. With n_gram = 2 the network equals build_ftna().

Usage

build_ngram(
  data,
  start = FALSE,
  end = FALSE,
  actor = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  session = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  time_threshold = 900,
  timezone = "UTC",
  state_cols = NULL,
  metadata_cols = NULL,
  n_gram = 2L,
  group = NULL,
  scaling = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  labels = NULL,
  params = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

The sequences: a data frame with one row per sequence and one column per position, or an event log (one row per event, with action set).

start

A start state put before every sequence, so the network shows where sequences begin (an edge from it to each sequence's first state). FALSE (default) adds none, TRUE adds one labelled "Start", and a single string adds one with that label. One-hot data, whose rows are time points rather than sequences, raises an error.

end

An end state put in the cell after each sequence's last observed state, so the network shows where sequences stop. It has no outgoing edges and no self-loop, unlike mark_terminal_state(), which fills all trailing missing cells with an absorbing state. FALSE (default), TRUE ("End") or a single string, as start.

actor

The column naming who each row belongs to (a person, a team). In an event log, each actor's events form a sequence, split further by session or time_threshold; in one-hot data, each actor's rows. Default NULL.

action

The column holding each event's state; setting it declares the data an event log. Column names give no role: action, actor, time and session are read only when set. A column called Action with nothing declared raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, and an undeclared time or session column beside action is named in a message of class nestimate_column_role. Default NULL.

time

The timestamp column of an event log. Events are ordered by it, and a gap longer than time_threshold starts a new sequence. Default NULL.

session

The column identifying sessions in an event log; each session is its own sequence, also without actor. Default NULL.

order

The column that orders events sharing a timestamp; without it, those events keep their row order. Default NULL.

time_threshold

The longest gap, in seconds, between two events of the same sequence in an event log; a longer gap starts a new sequence. FALSE turns the split off, so each actor (or actor-session) is one sequence. Default 900.

timezone

The Olson time zone for timestamps without an offset (passed to prepare()); timestamps with an offset, such as ...Z or +02:00, are converted from it. Default "UTC".

state_cols

The columns of a wide table that are sequence positions; every other column goes to the network's metadata. Declared columns are positions even when they hold only 0 and 1. With nothing declared, the frame must be one column or hold position columns named as a numbered run (a shared prefix and a number, T1, T2, ..., or 1, 2, ...); numeric columns beside the run and character or factor columns outside it are then covariates. Any other frame, and columns of only 0 and 1, raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input: nothing says whether they are positions or one-hot codes. Default NULL.

metadata_cols

Columns to keep as the network's metadata (covariates), never as positions; they cannot overlap state_cols. A column left out of a numbered run of positions is named in a message of class nestimate_column_role, and listing it here or in state_cols settles it. Default NULL.

n_gram

The window length, a whole number of at least 2. Default 2.

group

A column to split the data by: one network per value, returned as a netobject_group. Default NULL.

scaling

Rescaling applied to the weights after estimation, in the order given: "minmax" rescales the weights to run from 0 to 1, over every cell for the transition methods (tna's rule, so with no zero cell the smallest weight becomes 0) and over the non-zero weights, into (0, 1], for the other methods, "max" divides by the largest absolute weight, "rank" replaces the non-zero weights by their ranks, and "normalize" makes each row's absolute weights sum to 1; an undirected network whose matrix it makes asymmetric becomes directed, so both of a pair's values are kept as edges. Zero weights stay zero under every option. Combine them as in c("rank", "minmax"). Default NULL (none).

threshold

Weights whose absolute value is below this are set to zero. Default 0 (none).

labels

New display labels for the nodes, applied after estimation: a two-column data frame (name, label), a named character vector c(name = "label") or a named list. It rewrites the node labels and the weight matrix's dimnames; nodes not listed keep their names. Default NULL.

params

Settings for the estimator, as a named list, as for build_tna(); also duration (one value per position, accumulated into times) or time_matrix (one row per sequence, one column per position), which measure the distance in time instead of positions. Default list().

...

Further arguments for build_network(): format ("auto", "wide", "long" or "onehot", to force a reading of data), and for event logs prepare()'s time options unix_time_unit, is_unix_time and custom_format. method cannot be given: each alias has its own (error of class nestimate_bad_input).

Value

A netobject (a netobject_group with group), as build_network() returns it.

References

Tikka, S., López-Pernas, S., & Saqr, M. (2025). tna: An R package for transition network analysis. Applied Psychological Measurement. doi:10.1177/01466216251348840

See also

build_network() for every method; build_gap() and build_reverse() for the other tna model types.

Examples

build_network(trajectories, method = "ngram", n_gram = 3)
#> Network (method: ngram) [directed]
#>   Weights: [38.000, 861.000]  |  mean: 357.667
#> 
#>   Strongest edges (9 of 9):
#>    from       to         weight
#>    Active     Active     861   
#>    Average    Average    853   
#>    Active     Average    324   
#>    Disengaged Disengaged 292   
#>    Average    Active     285   
#>    Average    Disengaged 266   
#>    Disengaged Average    233   
#>    Disengaged Active      67   
#>    Active     Disengaged  38    
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix;
#>   extract_initial_probs() the initial probabilities.
build_ngram(trajectories, n_gram = 3)
#> Network (method: ngram) [directed]
#>   Weights: [38.000, 861.000]  |  mean: 357.667
#> 
#>   Strongest edges (9 of 9):
#>    from       to         weight
#>    Active     Active     861   
#>    Average    Average    853   
#>    Active     Average    324   
#>    Disengaged Disengaged 292   
#>    Average    Active     285   
#>    Average    Disengaged 266   
#>    Disengaged Average    233   
#>    Disengaged Active      67   
#>    Active     Disengaged  38    
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix;
#>   extract_initial_probs() the initial probabilities.
